objective: Build a model-assisted player props research tool around explicit member jobs, using proven information architecture without copying a competitor's brand or inventing unavailable data.
shellDecision: Keep the shared OddSphere product navigation and max-w-7xl frame consistent across Daily Edge, Player Props, Tracking, My Bets, and Account.

sources.bestFeature: A guided path from trending or curated props into performance, matchup, injury, line-movement, and best-price context.
sources.oddsphereUse: Make broad prop discovery and filtering the default, then move supporting evidence behind the selected prop.

sources.bestFeature: One player and one line anchor the research screen, with recent-performance views doing most of the explanatory work.
sources.oddsphereUse: Use a single selected prop as the visual anchor; reserve trend charts until verified game-log data exists.

sources.bestFeature: A filter-first positive-EV scanner sorted by profit margin with the executable sportsbook price visible.
sources.oddsphereUse: Keep model signals, price comparison, and dense controls inside one configurable market board.

sources.bestFeature: Linked widgets and preset workspaces distinguish monitoring from analysis while keeping the primary number dominant.
sources.oddsphereUse: Use one stable workspace with linked evidence modules, while preserving the existing shared app shell.

sources.bestFeature: Muted navigation, compact tabs, and fewer borders allow hierarchy to be felt instead of announced.
sources.oddsphereUse: Use one quiet explorer control zone, restrained accents, and progressive disclosure for secondary evidence.

sources.bestFeature: Player research is organized into distinct thematic views for season stats, splits, logs, and comparisons.
sources.oddsphereUse: Let search or the player directory open a focused player workspace without introducing another navigation mode.

sources.bestFeature: Dense operational data stays scannable through search, filters, and consistent player columns.
sources.oddsphereUse: Keep the market board compact and sortable without grouping the universe by recommendation grade.

userJobs: Explore the full loaded player-prop market without being pushed toward a pick.
Compare the model projection with the sportsbook line.
See the best available sportsbook price.
Understand why OddSphere differs from the market and what may change.
Scan every market, grade, team, book, and start time when needed.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: Where am I in OddSphere and how do I move to another product?
sectionAudit.decision: Keep the existing OddSphere top bar, icons, dimensions, and max-w-7xl frame unchanged.
passCriteria: Player Props is visibly active.
The shell matches Daily Edge and does not introduce a props-only header style.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: What slate am I viewing and is there anything worth opening?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: A compact context header with the most decision-relevant summary values.
sectionAudit.decision: Use a compact slate strip for date, matchup, first pitch, probable pitchers, loaded prop count, books, and freshness; keep provider operations admin-only.
passCriteria: A member can identify the slate without scrolling.
No provider, fixture, database, or publishing-control copy appears.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: How do I narrow the loaded market universe to the players, markets, and books I care about?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: One global search, quick market filters, and configurable price coverage.
sectionAudit.decision: Use one Prop Researcher with player, team, market, and sportsbook search; quick market filters; and a direct path into focused player workspaces.
passCriteria: Search and market navigation are the primary entry point.
Model signals are filters rather than a competing destination.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: Which parts of the slate are worth investigating, and for what reason?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: Curated discovery that opens into research without claiming to be a definitive pick list.
sectionAudit.decision: Surface a projection gap, a cross-book price spread, and a context-dependent market; use model signal only as supporting metadata.
passCriteria: Radar cards represent different research questions rather than a ranking.
Every Radar card opens the same Prop Reader used by the full board.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: What player markets are loaded, and how does the model compare with each current line and price?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: A filterable prop finder with at-a-glance market and model comparison.
sectionAudit.decision: Use one continuous board with player, market, side and line, projection, book price, edge, EV, confidence, and model signal.
passCriteria: Every inspectable model state remains available in the same board.
The board defaults to a neutral player sort rather than model rank.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: What makes this prop visually memorable if a licensed portrait is unavailable?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: Use the primary decision number as the visual anchor.
sectionAudit.decision: Replace initials with a projection-versus-line panel, team mark, market code, and matchup status; preserve the local licensed-image contract.
passCriteria: No oversized initials or fake portrait appears.
The panel communicates projection, line, direction, team, and market without invented data.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: What props are loaded for my favorite player?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: Dedicated player pages organized by thematic market views.
sectionAudit.decision: Search a player or select them from the player directory to open a focused player workspace.
passCriteria: One search control handles player discovery.
The workspace preserves every loaded market, projection, price, signal, and Reader access point for that player.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: What did my board search find?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: Selected player and line dominate; supporting modules are linked and secondary.
sectionAudit.decision: Filter the market board in place and use the centered Prop Reader for focused interpretation.
passCriteria: Search does not introduce a second navigation system.
Each result keeps a direct path to projection, market comparison, price, and context.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: How can I inspect the complete board with my own criteria?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: Filter-first dense scanner with stable columns and execution price.
sectionAudit.decision: Expose the primary research controls first, keep advanced filters collapsed, and do not group rows by recommendation grade.
passCriteria: Desktop columns support fast model-versus-market comparison.
Mobile cards remain complete and tappable without horizontal overflow.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: How does the model compare with the market, where is the best price, and what can change the read?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: Centered analytical workspace with primary evidence before methodology.
sectionAudit.decision: Use a centered desktop Reader and full-screen mobile Reader with a plain-English lead summary followed by model comparison, projection, price, confidence, change risks, and matchup context.
passCriteria: No right-side desktop drawer remains.
The member sees evidence and caveats without raw model or provider diagnostics.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: How does the model currently classify this prop?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: Compact analytical labels that can be filtered without replacing the underlying data.
sectionAudit.decision: Show Best Angle, Lean, Watchlist, No Edge, Pending, and Research as one board column and filter.
passCriteria: Signals do not create a separate pick feed.
Signal colors align with Daily Edge: emerald Best Angle, sky Lean, indigo Watchlist, gray No Edge.

sectionAudit.userQuestion: Which information belongs to operators rather than members?
sectionAudit.benchmarkPattern: Operational diagnostics stay behind an administrative boundary.
sectionAudit.decision: Keep providers, raw reason codes, source data, feature inventories, shrinkage, settlement, and CLV in admin review only.
passCriteria: Member and preview modes contain no operational narration.
Admin review preserves all required audit fields.

rejectedPatterns: Do not fabricate L5, L10, L20, matchup, split, or line-movement charts before verified data exists.
Do not scrape or hotlink unlicensed player portraits; accept only verified local licensed assets.
Do not show oversized initials as a substitute for a player portrait.
Do not imply bet placement, saved picks, public publishing, or persistence that is not implemented.
Do not expose provider health, database state, fixture mechanics, or raw model internals to members.
Do not change the shared top navigation to make one feature look separately branded.
